body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 21, 2026 — a day that starts with a major incident on the Grapevine after a semi truck and trailer fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine, tying up traffic for hours. We’re looking at a high near 101° today with air quality at 108 — unhealthy for sensitive groups. Let’s get you caught up on the night and the day ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident unfolded just before 1 a.m. when a semi truck and trailer became fully engulfed in the number three lane of northbound I-5 south of Grapevine. CHP and Engine 56 were on scene quickly, establishing command as the Tejon Incident. The fire burned for hours: by 6 a.m. crews were still working it, a heavy-duty tow had been called in, and traffic was backing up to the Lebec service route. Earlier, around 10:34 p.m., a quarter-acre brush fire on McCombs Road (State Route 43 north of Wasco) was burning with a fast rate of spread and potential to run west. Multiple engines and a water tender responded, additional wildland equipment was ordered, and crews split into Division Bravo and Division Yankee for what command described as a lengthy mop-up. Just after 3 a.m., two subjects were on a Woodford Boulevard property behind a white pickup, possibly taking items. The subjects were known to be in possession of firearms, though none were visible at first; officers later made contact and located a firearm. Around 9:50 p.m., a robbery at gunpoint was reported on Denise Avenue in north Bakersfield. The suspect was described as a transient white male in his late 30s, wearing a baseball cap and black face mask, pulling a wagon, and accompanied by a white female. Around 4:36 a.m., three subjects at a trucking yard south of Gibson Street were reported possibly taking items. Deputies set a perimeter and the subjects ran — one headed south toward a fence with an officer holding the hole. One subject was described as known to carry a knife.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 101° and a low around 74° tonight. It’s currently 99° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 108 — unhealthy for sensitive groups. 

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Bakersfield police are seeking the public’s help identifying suspects in a White Lane burglary. The burglary occurred on White Lane, and police are asking anyone with information to come forward. This incident follows a series of property crimes in the area, and police believe tips from the community could help solve the case.

**23ABC told us that** the California Highway Patrol has confirmed new details in the deadly Highway 99 crash from early Sunday morning. CHP confirmed the BMW involved in the crash was the vehicle traveling northbound in the southbound lanes at the time of the collision. Initial reports indicated the Honda Accord was at fault. All other aspects of the crash remain under investigation, including potential charges. The Kern County Coroner’s Office confirmed 41-year-old Vanessa Sue Wetmore, 20-year-old Kylie Wetmore, and 16-year-old Kloie Wetmore died in the crash. The crash happened just after midnight Sunday, Aug. 16, on southbound Highway 99, north of Seventh Standard Road. CHP says three vehicles were involved: a 2022 Honda Accord driven by an unidentified female, a 2019 BMW 530i driven by a 44-year-old male, and a 2022 Chevrolet Colorado driven by a 41-year-old female. The impact caused the Honda to burst into flames, killing the three people inside. The driver of the BMW sustained major injuries and was transported to the hospital. The two people in the Chevrolet Colorado sustained minor injuries. Investigators say it is still unknown whether drugs or alcohol played a role in the crash. The investigation is still ongoing and CHP is asking anyone with information about the crash to call (661) 396-6600.

**According to KGET 17,** Flood Ministries is celebrating 20 years of helping Kern County families find hope and stability. The organization has been a valuable resource for the community over the past two decades, providing support and services to those in need. This milestone highlights the ongoing commitment of Flood Ministries to making a positive impact in Kern County.

**23ABC said that** NAMI Kern County will celebrate its 20th annual 'NAMIWalks' this October at the Park at Riverwalk. The annual event aims to connect our local community members with resources for themselves or their loved ones who may be struggling with their mental health. What started two decades ago as an event with only a handful of vendors has now grown into what it is today. NAMI Kern County announced that the theme for this year’s walk is “Together, We Are NAMIWalks.” The organization expects up to 40 vendors this year, and around 1,000 participants in the walk itself.

**KGET 17 announced that** a Foothill High School graduate has won a $25,000 scholarship to attend his dream school. Eric Ventura was awarded the California Table Grape Scholarship after applying last October. After months of waiting, he learned he won the $25,000 award, which will be spread across his four years at UC Berkeley. Ventura credits the nonprofit Youth 2 Leaders with helping him and his parents navigate the process.

**Bakersfield Now reports that** a 32-year-old Bakersfield man has died of dehydration tied to heat exposure. The Kern County Coroner’s Office has identified the man, and the incident highlights the dangers of extreme heat in our area.

## Something good

Flood Ministries is celebrating 20 years of helping Kern County families find hope and stability. The organization has been a valuable resource for the community over the past two decades, providing support and services to those in need. This milestone highlights the ongoing commitment of Flood Ministries to making a positive impact in Kern County.

## Coming up this week

On Tuesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m., and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater will host several events this week: Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22; Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 on August 24; Rodney Carrington on August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28; Willie Barcena on August 29; and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.
